newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends higher on physical buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends higher on physical buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended higher on Thursday compared to New York's Wednesday close on strong speculative buying and physical demand, dampened slightly by profit-taking later in the session, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$355.50/356.00 an ounce, up from New York's US$354.00/50 close on Wednesday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$353.50/354.00.
"The market crawled up gradually during the day on a weaker dollar/yen," said a dealer at a local securities house.
"Market sentiment had turned bullish after gold held at US$350 support levels and surged on the palladium and platinum prices," a dealer said.
Dealers expected the price to continue trending higher.
Local gold ended HK$17 higher at HK$3,288 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to zero from its previous fix at +5.00.
